newsitem.title: USA: Banamex sees 2 bln peso/yr hit from mortgage plan.
newsitem.headline: Banamex sees 2 bln peso/yr hit from mortgage plan.

text.p: Mexican bank Banamex, a unit of Grupo Financiero Banamex-Accival said on Wednesday it saw a 2 billion peso a year impact on net interest income from its new mortgage discount plan.
However, bank officials said the impact will be more than offset by loan loss privisions.

While "$250 million dollars will be the impact (each year) on net interest income...we expect that it will be more than compensated in loan loss provisions," Jorge Hierro, head of investor relations, told a Smith Barney conference here on Latin American equities.
Hierro said the bank's net interest income could fall 15-20 percent. He said total net interest income from mortgages was about 10 bln pesos and that the plan would reduce it by two billion pesos.
Banamex on Tuesday unveiled a plan granting discounts of up to 25 percent for mortgage clients if they have 12 consecutive on-time payments.
Hierro said the bank has already raised $1.1 billion in its initial phase of recapitalization, which he said would be completed by year's end.
The bank's second phase of recapitalization is aimed at attracting an additional $500 million, of which $150 million has already been raised, he said.
"We will get it from source one, source two and source three, I can't add much more than that. We are working on it," he said.
"We are very confident we will be able to do that without major dilution to shareholders," he said.

Asked about whether the recap would imply any dilution, he said: "We are aware we have acheived the first phase of our recap without any dilution. We have set a very tough standard. All i can say is that we will do our best,"
